name: Fault line
description: Algorithmic: motion loads stress until it slips — the pulse rate shatters downward across all four segments, each climbing back at its own speed
author: ShockingVRC

kind.text:
Motion loads stress like a fault: velocity, acceleration and recoil — and a slow creep — charge it. When it passes the fault's strength, set by depth and drifting with a noise that recoil stirs, it slips and resets, so the intervals follow your motion and never settle into a pattern.
How far: the drop is proportional to the stress released — deep presses give rarer, larger slips.
Shatter: the drop splits across the four 25 ms segments. Each lands at its own random share and climbs back at its own speed — segment 1 by depth, 2 by velocity, 3 by acceleration, 4 by recoil — and each segment's intensity sinks with its fall, more after recoil and fast strokes. Depth keeps it low longer; velocity shortens the stay. The top wanders through 82–100 Hz.
Sliders: Max frequency drop caps every fall (Hz). Max device power is Limit Max on both channels — 6 to start; the Graph cap in Setup still wins. B plays the segments mirrored.
